data.outcome_summary: PIRLS 2011 International Results in Reading reports fourth-grade reading comprehension achievement on the PIRLS 0–1,000 scale (centerpoint 500) and presents results for 49 participating systems plus nine benchmarking participants, with some countries assessing sixth grade and three prePIRLS participants. The assessment measures two purposes (literary experience; acquire and use information) and four comprehension processes (retrieve explicitly stated information; straightforward inferences; interpret/integrate; examine/evaluate), with benchmark cutpoints at 400, 475, 550, and 625. The report summarizes cross-country differences in average achievement, trends since PIRLS 2001 and 2006, gender gaps (girls higher by 16 points on average at fourth grade), and the distribution of students reaching each benchmark (e.g., Singapore 24% at Advanced; median Low benchmark attainment 95%). It also links achievement patterns to home and school context scales (e.g., home resources, early literacy activities, preprimary attendance, school resource shortages, school emphasis on academic success). The excerpt does not provide an ML modeling pipeline; therefore, no predictive performance metrics or PV/missing-data handling for estimation are reported here.
